correctness.rationale: For each vertex, the sharp \(\ell_\infty\) row norm follows by phase choice in a finite kernel. Each common-coordinate centered Bernoulli law is convexly dominated by the rare-coordinate law with support endpoints −1,(1−a)/a; the secant inequality proves this even for complex multipliers through t↦|s+ct|. Conditional replacement is valid for independent variables, proves a common maximizing vertex, and yields the formula. The homogeneous identity follows from an exact one-step binomial telescoping formula valid at integer means and \(n=1\). Fixed-bias asymptotics use \(L^2\) uniform integrability and the normal CLT; sparse asymptotics use binomial local probabilities. A standalone checker independently exercises 126 rational inequalities, 60 exact homogeneous identities and 62 complex inequalities, without substituting enumeration for proof.

value.rationale: The sharp endpoint norm of a first-chaos diagonal multiplier on a nonuniform finite product probability space is a natural Banach-operator invariant. Identifying one measure-determined maximizing row for all complex coefficient vectors is a structural simplification of the full \(2^n\)-vertex optimization; it yields every heterogeneously biased norm by one expectation and an exact closed form with distinct \(\sqrt n\) and n growth regimes for the canonical projection. These are motivated analytic boundaries rather than arbitrary numerical cases or mere restatements of uniform-cube formulas.
